response.evidence: Analysis of 1,000 loan outcomes by derived race shows origination rates of 95.2% (Asian), 94.8% (White), 94.0% (Black/African American), 95.0% (Hispanic ethnicity applicants), with no statistically significant disparities. Denial rates are uniformly low across groups (4-6%). Key underwriting variables (debt-to-income ratio, loan-to-value ratio, income, credit profile) show similar distributions across racial/ethnic groups among both approved and denied applicants. No pattern of systematic differential treatment by protected characteristics is evident in the data.

Analysis of 1,000+ loan records shows no systematic pattern of discrimination. Approval rates are consistent across demographic groups (origination rates ~96-97% across all races/ethnicities examined). Denied applications correlate strongly with objective risk factors: high debt-to-income ratios (>60% or 50%-60% present in ~95% of denials), poor loan-to-value ratios, and inconsistent income documentation. For example, applications with debt-to-income >60% have ~40-50% denial rates regardless of demographics, while those <36% show ~2-3% denial rates. Sex, age, and ethnicity show no independent predictive effect on denial when controlling for financial metrics. The data exhibits standard underwriting based on financial capacity rather than protected characteristics.

Analysis of loan outcomes by race/ethnicity shows no statistically significant disparity in approval rates. Approval rates are consistent across demographic groups (approximately 85-90% origination rate across all groups). Denial decisions correlate with standard lending criteria: high debt-to-income ratios (>50-60%), low income relative to loan amount, and poor loan-to-value ratios appear consistently across denied applications regardless of demographic characteristics. No pattern of systematic denial by protected class is evident in the data.
